title: Bracketed polynomial root
prompt: Implement solve(payload) for a polynomial supplied as coefficients in descending-power order, with numeric lo, hi, and tolerance. Evaluate with Horner's rule and return {"root": x}. Find a root by bisection only: if an endpoint is exactly a root, return that endpoint; otherwise the endpoint signs must differ. Maintain the bracket until its width is at most 2*tolerance, and return its midpoint (an exactly zero midpoint may return immediately). Use at most 200 iterations. Return {"error":"invalid_bounds"} for lo>hi, {"error":"invalid_tolerance"} for tolerance<=0, {"error":"not_bracketed"} when neither endpoint is zero and their signs do not differ, and {"error":"not_converged"} if 200 iterations do not reach the tolerance. Check bounds before tolerance. Coefficients are a nonempty list and all values are finite; supported valid brackets converge within 200 iterations. A root inside a same-sign bracket is intentionally not searched for. Do not mutate input. Root grading uses absolute tolerance 1e-6 and relative tolerance 1e-8.
